title: Will AI kill startups? Avoiding the "turkey graph" and building defensibility against the labs
summary: Paul Buchheit explains which startups AI labs will run over and which stay defensible. Building on a lab's roadmap, or on workarounds for today's model limits, is a trap. Network effects and existing distribution are the moat when software becomes trivially clonable.

principles.text: Startups building on a lab's roadmap or adjacent to its core business will get run over.
principles.quote: startups that are building on someone else's you know, on Anthropic's road map, I think are going to get run over.

principles.text: A thriving business that is easy to take from you is a 'turkey graph' startup: great numbers right up until the day it's chopped.
principles.quote: if you have a great business that's making, you know, $100 million, uh but it's easy for someone else to take that business from you, uh you're you're a turkey graph startup.

principles.text: Don't build middleware that patches today's model deficiencies; you're implicitly betting the models won't improve.
principles.quote: the issue with a lot of software startups, I think, is they're sort of betting that the models won't just fix all the stuff that's wrong with them.

principles.text: Test defensibility by imagining next year's model and competing against yourself as an ambitious 19-year-old.
principles.quote: Think about it as though you already had the future AI, um and then compete with yourself.

principles.text: If your moat is that software is hard to build, you're in trouble; the moat should be that everyone already uses it.
principles.quote: if the moat is that it's hard for someone else to to clone your product, you're you're in trouble. Generally, you want a product where the strength comes from the fact that everyone is already using it.

principles.text: Network effects and marketplaces survive cloning: a copied app without supply or customers is worthless.
principles.quote: If you could hypothetically just completely open source your product, give it away, and it wouldn't make much of a difference.
